skill.name: sast-horusec
skill.description: Use Horusec to run multi-language static application security testing, secret history checks, CI security scans, and vulnerability triage across software projects.
skill.summary: Run Horusec SAST scans and triage security findings across mixed-language repositories.
skill.author: AgentSecOps

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown examples, rule templates, and defensive security references. The confirmed risks are unsafe installation and Docker guidance: remote scripts piped to shell, Docker socket exposure, and broad Docker socket permission changes.

remediation.issue: Remote installer scripts are piped directly to bash in SKILL.md and the CI template.
remediation.suggestion: Replace pipe-to-shell installs with pinned release downloads, checksum verification, or package manager instructions that verify integrity before execution.

remediation.issue: Docker examples mount /var/run/docker.sock into the scanning container.
remediation.suggestion: Avoid Docker socket mounts. Use rootless Docker, isolated runners, read-only source mounts, or non-Docker Horusec execution where possible.

remediation.issue: Troubleshooting guidance suggests world-writable Docker socket permissions.
remediation.suggestion: Remove chmod 666 guidance and document safer Docker group membership, least-privilege runners, or temporary isolated environments.

remediation.issue: CI examples rely on mutable third-party actions, images, and remote installer scripts.
remediation.suggestion: Pin actions and container images to immutable SHAs or digests, and document update review procedures for CI dependencies.

content.value_statement: Security teams need consistent SAST scans across mixed-language repositories. This skill guides Horusec scans, CI integration, secret history checks, and result triage.
actual_capabilities: Guide local Horusec scans with text, JSON, or SonarQube-compatible output.
Enable git history analysis for exposed secrets and credential review.
Show CI integration patterns for GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, and Jenkins.
Explain false positive management with accepted hashes and ignored paths.
Help parse and prioritize Horusec findings by severity and language.
Provide configuration examples for timeouts, custom rules, and custom images.
limitations: Requires Horusec CLI or Docker to run actual scans.
Does not replace human validation of security findings.
Coverage depends on Horusec analyzers and their supported languages.
Does not automatically fix vulnerabilities in source code.

use_cases.title: Check Code Before a Pull Request
use_cases.description: Run a local Horusec scan, review high-severity findings, and confirm fixes before opening a pull request.

use_cases.title: Build a Secure CI Gate
use_cases.description: Add Horusec scanning to CI and fail builds when findings exceed the selected severity threshold.

use_cases.title: Triage Application Security Findings
use_cases.description: Review JSON scan results, group findings by severity, and document accepted false positives for audit trails.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Basic Scan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Horusec SAST skill to scan this repository locally. Explain the command, expected output, and how to review high-severity findings.

prompt_templates.title: Review Secret History
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through a Horusec git history secret scan. Include how to handle exposed credentials and what evidence to document.

prompt_templates.title: Add CI Enforcement
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Horusec CI scanning plan for my project. Include severity thresholds, report artifacts, and pull request feedback.

prompt_templates.title: Tune Findings at Scale
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me tune Horusec for a monorepo with multiple languages. Include custom rules, ignored paths, timeout settings, and false positive governance.

output_examples.input: Scan a Python service before release.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends a local Horusec scan, export of a structured report, review of critical and high findings, and a re-scan after fixes.

output_examples.input: Add SAST to a pull request workflow.
output: The workflow runs on pull requests and scheduled scans.
Reports are saved as artifacts for audit review.
The build can fail when findings meet the configured threshold.

output_examples.input: Reduce false positives from test fixtures.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests reviewing each finding, recording accepted hashes, excluding low-value paths, and revisiting accepted risk regularly.

best_practices: Run scans before merging code and after security-sensitive changes.
Store reports as restricted artifacts because findings may include sensitive code context.
Rotate any credential found in source or git history before closing the finding.
anti_patterns: Do not ignore findings only because they appear in test or vendor paths.
Do not publish scan reports to public logs or unrestricted artifacts.
Do not rely on SAST alone for runtime or authorization issues.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It helps plan and run Horusec SAST scans, review findings, configure CI checks, and manage false positives.

faq.question: Does it run Horusec automatically?
faq.answer: It provides commands and workflow guidance. Actual execution depends on your environment and installed tools.

faq.question: Can it detect secrets in git history?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for enabling Horusec git history analysis and responding to exposed credentials.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Will it fix vulnerabilities for me?
faq.answer: No. It helps identify and prioritize issues, but developers must apply and validate fixes.

faq.question: What should I protect after a scan?
faq.answer: Protect scan reports, logs, and artifacts because they can contain source paths, vulnerable snippets, and secret indicators.
